architecture_decisions.recommendation: Centralized event handler resolution through a single _get_event_handler method that handles both Event objects and dotted handler name strings
architecture_decisions.rationale: The upload component previously had its own logic to parse handler names, get substates, and retrieve event handlers. This duplicated logic existed in multiple places. By extending _get_event_handler to accept both Event objects and string handler names, we create a single source of truth for event handler resolution, reducing code duplication and ensuring consistency.
alternatives_considered: Creating a separate function for string-based handler resolution
Keeping the upload-specific logic isolated in app.py
Creating a new utility function specifically for upload handlers

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Moved StateProxy wrapping from _get_event_handler to the calling context, specifically only for background tasks
architecture_decisions.rationale: Previously, _get_event_handler automatically wrapped the substate in StateProxy for background tasks. This created a tight coupling between handler resolution and background task handling. By moving the StateProxy wrapping to the calling context (both in _process and _process_background), we separate concerns: _get_event_handler only resolves handlers, while callers decide how to handle the state based on handler properties. This makes the code more modular and easier to reason about.
alternatives_considered: Creating separate methods for background vs non-background handler resolution
Using a flag parameter to control StateProxy wrapping

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained consistent error handling for background tasks in upload handlers by checking event_handler.is_background directly
architecture_decisions.rationale: The upload component needs to reject background event handlers since upload operations require immediate file handling. By using the centralized event_handler object retrieved via _get_event_handler, we maintain the same validation logic while eliminating duplicate code. This ensures consistent behavior across all event types.
alternatives_considered: Creating a separate validation function for upload handlers
Adding a special flag to EventHandler for upload compatibility
Moving the validation logic to the EventHandler class itself

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed direct EventHandler import from reflex.event in app.py since it's no longer needed after refactoring
architecture_decisions.rationale: The upload handler resolution no longer needs to directly inspect EventHandler objects since _get_event_handler returns the handler object. This reduces dependencies and keeps the code cleaner. The EventHandler type is still used internally by the framework but not needed at this abstraction level.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the import for type hints

tickets.title: Refactor upload component to use centralized event handler resolution
tickets.description: Update the upload file handling logic in app.py to use the existing _get_event_handler method instead of duplicating handler resolution logic. This includes parsing handler names, getting substates, and retrieving event handlers.

tickets.title: Extend _get_event_handler to support string-based handler resolution
tickets.description: Modify the _get_event_handler method in state.py to accept both Event objects and dotted handler name strings. This enables the method to be used by both regular event processing and the upload component which receives handler names as strings.

tickets.title: Decouple StateProxy wrapping from handler resolution
tickets.description: Move StateProxy wrapping logic out of _get_event_handler and into the calling contexts (_process and _process_background). This separates handler resolution from state proxying concerns, making the code more modular.

implementation_summary:
The changes implement a consolidation of event handler resolution logic by extending the existing _get_event_handler method to serve both regular event processing and the upload component. Previously, the upload component in app.py had its own logic to parse handler names, navigate substates, and retrieve event handlers, which duplicated functionality already present in state.py.

The key architectural decision was to make _get_event_handler polymorphic - it now accepts either an Event object or a dotted handler name string. This allows the upload component to leverage the same robust handler resolution logic while maintaining its specific validation requirements (rejecting background handlers). The method signature was updated to return BaseState instead of BaseState | StateProxy, moving the StateProxy wrapping responsibility to the calling context.

Another important change was the decoupling of StateProxy wrapping from handler resolution. Previously, _get_event_handler automatically wrapped the state in StateProxy for background tasks. This created unnecessary coupling. Now, _get_event_handler only resolves the handler, and the calling code (both in _process and _process_background) decides whether to wrap the state based on handler.is_background. This separation of concerns makes the code more maintainable and follows the single responsibility principle.

The implementation maintains backward compatibility while reducing code duplication. All existing functionality is preserved, including error handling for background tasks in upload handlers. The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing reactive state management system, ensuring consistent event handling patterns across the framework.
